bilateralMAINComparisons.leftToRight: 78 identifies an institution maintaining a collection and lending access.28 already names the library as a premise and asks which circulation operation a reader performs when taking a selected book home for its loan period, distinguishing new checkout from return/renewal/hold.28 does not ask which institution lends books;78 does not select the stage of a circulation transaction.
bilateralMAINComparisons.rightToLeft: In28 the institution stays the same across all answer operations; its key depends on a newly started temporary loan.78 would still identify the library for a reader who reserves/returns materials. These are institution/function and transaction-state predicates, not direct reverse questions of one named relation.

bilateralMAINComparisons.leftToRight: 78 institution retains a collection for readers use/lending;79 enterprise offers books for sale. Temporary access to retained holdings versus commercial sale is a different relation and identifies a different organizational function.
bilateralMAINComparisons.rightToLeft: 79 asks the retailer selling books, not a collecting/lending institution;78 does not ask which business transfers books through sale. Shared book subject matter/option pool does not equate these MAIN facts.

bilateralMAINComparisons.leftToRight: 78 collection/use/lending of resources;80 organization prepares manuscript publication and coordinates its release. Access/custody of resources versus editorial selection/publication organization are different stages and responsibilities.
bilateralMAINComparisons.rightToLeft: 80 asks who organizes publication before readers obtain a finished edition.78 asks who collects materials and lends them after acquisition. A publisher need not maintain a lending collection; a library need not publish the manuscripts it acquires.

bilateralMAINComparisons.leftToRight: 78 identifies collection/lending institution;actual81 identifies physical manufacturer printing and binding a run. Acquisition/custody/access to existing resources differs from fabrication of copies.
bilateralMAINComparisons.rightToLeft: Actual81 asks the enterprise producing printed copies and binding, not who retains a fund for readers.78 includes no manufacture condition, so reversing the cards does not ask the same operation.

bilateralMAINComparisons.leftToRight: 78 is an institution/collection offering lending access. MiddleAges50 asks a type of document compilation containing copies of charters/institutional documents, a cartulary used to preserve evidence of rights/holdings. Preserving a compilation and naming a reader-service institution are different entities/relations.
bilateralMAINComparisons.rightToLeft: The cartulary prompt names a bound archival-document compilation and asks its genre/type; it does not ask where readers borrow books. A library can hold a cartulary, but that containment does not make either MAIN a reverse definition of the other.
